newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee recovers to end at 35.89/90 vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee recovers to end at 35.89/90 vs dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed steady at 35.89/90 against the dollar on Friday after touching a low of 35.92 in afternoon trade, dealers said.
The spot dollar market was steady until 1415 hours local when a large Calcutta bank entered the market to buy at 35.90.
Just as the market steadied, the Calcutta bank hit again, this time buying upto 35.92 level, dealers said.
Sensing unfulfilled demand from the Calcutta bank, local banks also began buying dollars, dealers said.

Even as local banks were bidding for dollars, the same Calcutta bank made its third entry, this time to sell dollars, dealers said. "It took time for the market to realise this time they had come to sell dollars," said a dealer at an Indian bank.
"The market was in total confusion," the dealer said.
The Calcutta bank sold dollars at 35.89/91 levels.
As the market resolved the confusion and learned about the Calcutta bank's two-way purchases, the same bank was in the market again, buying dollars at 35.89/90.
The spot market closed at these levels.
The six month dollar premium closed the day at 7.19 percent, marginally down from the previous close of 7.25 percent.
